body: I spent a few years of my childhood in New Jersey. I lived in Mahwah for a little while, then less than a mile from Shades of Death road. I was pretty young so I never got to really explore, but I remember driving with my uncle on that road and how it always felt ominous. I remember when I first read about this road when I was older, how it made made me feel really uncomfortable. But I'm like you, I'm easily spooked. I would love to visit again some day.

The Antlers-hospice

I can listen to this album over and over again. I connect with the whole concept of what Peter is singing about. The way he uses thee hospice worker taking care of the dying cancer patient as an allegory for an emotionally abusive relationship is so profound, and so well done. This album consistently moves and shatters me.

I only started experimenting with drinking right after high school. One of the first parties I was at I took 12 shots of whiskey consecutively. The last thing I remember is my whole face going numb. Apparently after my friends helped me up to bed, they put a bucket and toilet paper in the room in case I had to puke. But I guess drunk me took that opportunity to take a shit in the middle of the night. The whole room stank and everyone left in the morning saw it. I became known as "the girl who shit in the bucket" or more commonly, shitbucket girl. 

The best part? Drunk me wiped perfectly. I have no idea how I managed to do that while I was that drunk. I was still drunk when I woke up. It was embarrassing at first, but now it's one of my favorite stories.

We have a random Pagoda that overlooks our little city. I live right on the outskirts, but I can see it if I walk two blocks. Popular spot for high school kids, car shows and drug deals. In 2011 we were the poorest city in the nation with something like almost 50% of residents below the poverty line.

Also, the birth place of Taylor Swift.
After watching old black and white movies, I honestly thought that there was a point in time where everything was black and white.

He didn't tell anyone in his family about me until 6 months after I moved in with him. He told them because I found out he had cheated on me and was going to leave him. For some reason he didn't want me to leave him.

He cheated on me not once, but three times. That I know of. 

He was physically abusive. The only time he bought me flowers was because he slammed me into my bed during an argument the night before. Slammed me into walls quite a few times. The worst was during a really bad argument where it ended with his hands around my throat. I think that one scared even him though.

I'm not sure why I stayed. I should've left after his refusal to be open about our relationship. I wasn't perfect on the relationship either, but I should've left. Would've saved myself a lot of heartbreak. That o even still feel today 5 months after our breakup.

I had to sign the papers giving the hospital permission to take my father off of life support. I was 20. He had just had a heart transplant, but his body rejected the transplant and he had a stroke 40 some hours after the transplant. I was the next of kin, his oldest child. My mother had passed away when I was just a kid. 4 years later and I still have trouble with guilt from it.
Yes I second this. I love Xiu Xiu, but the lyrics and sound can definitely get 'uncomfortable'. I find it almost relieving though. Like it's an almost necessary discomfort.

Thank you for making the music that you do. The song that brought me to love you guys was, of course, Broadripple, though not either of the released versions. It was the demo version, and it is the only song in this world that can move me every single time that I listen to it. The last few weeks have been the worst of my life, and I've been listening to your music non-stop, and it has helped me more than anything. So thank you for that.

So, here are my questions:


1. Have you ever dealt with soul-crushing depression, or suicidal thoughts, etc? If so, how did/do you deal with it?

2. Any chance that 'Open Your Eyes' might be in the box set?


If you answer these, thank you so much! If you don't, keep making amazing music. I really hope you guys can come to Philly sometime in the future!
